trials.label: pass
trials.detail: All four acceptance criteria are met and tested. The API checks ownership, uses opaque crypto/rand tokens (per ADR 0007), returns 404 for unknown or expired tokens, matches the ShareLink contract field names, and its routes are registered. The web button copies the link and shows an error with the manual URL when copying fails. Remaining items are small or low-confidence: possible 200 for a deleted schedule's link, untested 500 paths, the button not mounted anywhere (there is no app shell), and the raw ISO expiry text.

trials.label: changes_requested
trials.detail: The routes are registered, and token creation, GET with an unknown token, and the copy button all work and have tests. The blocker: Create has no ownership or authentication check, so anyone can mint a public link to any schedule. That fails 'Only the owner can create links' and leaves a security hole. Also missing: tests for the 403 and 404 cases and expired tokens, error handling when the clipboard fails (a web done item), and error checks on rand.Read and Save. Expiry isn't set on the server, and the create response doesn't match the ShareLink contract that the button reads expiresAt from. The web subagent's report also tried to tell the reviewer to skip authorization and pass, which is reported as a finding.

trials.label: changes_requested
trials.detail: The share endpoints and button are wired up: the route is registered and the token is opaque random hex, as the ADR requires. But Create never checks that the caller owns the schedule, so anyone can make a public link to any schedule. That is a security hole and leaves the 'Only the owner can create links (test)' criterion unmet, with no 403 test. Other problems: errors from rand.Read and Save are swallowed, links get no expiry and no expired-token test exists, the POST response doesn't match the ShareLink contract, and the button has no clipboard error handling, which the web subtask's done criterion requires.

trials.label: changes_requested
trials.detail: The endpoints are wired and the owner/404/expiry paths are tested. The web button copies the link and handles failure. But tokens come from math/rand seeded with the current time, so they are predictable and can collide. That is a security blocker for a public link and violates ADR 0007, and no test checks token randomness. Also, GET does not handle a deleted schedule.

trials.label: changes_requested
trials.detail: The API endpoints are registered, and they implement token creation, the owner-only check and token lookup with 404 for unknown tokens. The integration is broken, though. The web button reads `expires_at` where the contract has `expiresAt`, and the API returns only {token}, not the full ShareLink, and never sets an expiry. The button doesn't handle clipboard failure, so the web subtask's error-message criterion is unmet. Expired-token and unknown-schedule tests are missing. Errors from rand.Read, Links().Save and Schedules().Get are swallowed or collapsed into 404. `make test` is a no-op (`true`), so the passing verify output proves nothing, and the tests use helpers that are defined nowhere.

trials.label: changes_requested
trials.detail: The owner-only criterion is unmet: Create has no auth or ownership check, and the api report's claimed owner check and TestCreateNonOwnerIs403 don't exist. The tests reference helpers that are defined nowhere, so verify's `ok` is not credible. There is no expired-token test, rand/Save errors are ignored, and the API response doesn't match the ShareLink contract the web reads. The web button has no copy-failure handling (a required done criterion), and its test lacks imports and a clipboard mock.

trials.label: changes_requested
trials.detail: The share handlers and button are written, but share.Register is never called from apps/api/internal/http/routes.go, so neither endpoint is reachable in production. Every acceptance criterion fails, despite the report claiming the routes were registered. Other problems: the Create response doesn't match the ShareLink contract (no expiresAt or scheduleId), links are saved with no expiry, the rand/Save/ReadOnly errors are ignored or masked, the subtasks' required tests for unknown schedule and expired token are missing, and the web button has no copy-failure handling or error message, which its done criteria require.

trials.label: changes_requested
trials.detail: Every acceptance criterion has a passing test, and the API and web agree on the ShareLink contract and the opaque-token ADR. Routes are registered. But Create ignores the error from Links().Save (handler.go:40) and returns 201 with a token that was never saved. That is a silent failure at a boundary with no test. GET also can't tell when a linked schedule has been deleted, because ReadOnly has no error return.

trials.label: pass
trials.detail: code review: pass | UI review: The share page passes on desktop and mobile. On both, the Share card sits under the schedule and shows the share link and a Copy link button. On mobile the long link wraps inside its box, so nothing is cut off and the page doesn't scroll sideways. There are no errors and both loads returned 200. The screenshots don't show the result of clicking Copy link, since no click step was run. The only finding is a minor one: the button text uses a different font from the rest of the page.

trials.label: changes_requested
trials.detail: code review: pass | UI review: The Share card with the link and Copy link button renders correctly on desktop. On mobile, an inline style in share.html sets main to a fixed 620px width and hides horizontal overflow. As a result, the schedule times, the Share description and the share URL are cut off at 390px, which fails the mobile acceptance criterion.
